summary.headline: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 36.5% YoY to INR1,101.08 million, with order book up 20.4% QoQ to INR209 crores.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 36.5% YoY to INR1,101.08 million, with EBITDA excluding other income up 33.76% to INR141.54 million. EBITDA margin eased to 12.85% from 13.12%, which management attributed to higher raw material and employee costs as a share of sales. Standalone PAT fell YoY to INR99.79 million, but this reflects a one-time ~INR5 crore subsidiary dividend in the year-ago quarter. The order book reached INR209 crores at 30 June 2026, with more than 80% stated as executable in FY27, and a ~INR100 crore capacity expansion is coming on stream in phases at Nagpur.

segments.name: Heavy Engineering
segments.commentary: Order book of INR159 crores at 30 June 2026. Management says ~70% of heavy engineering is new project build and ~30% spare parts for installed base; capacity being raised from 9,000 to 18,000 metric tons.

segments.name: Wear Plates and Wear Parts
segments.commentary: Order book of INR26.42 crores. Management said growth in Q1 came across consumables, wear plates/parts and heavy engineering.

segments.name: Welding Consumables
segments.commentary: Order book of INR24.22 crores, described as a strong sequential increase driven by customers consolidating yearly requirements. Management said there was no one-off windfall.

segments.name: Defence
segments.commentary: Contributes approximately 1.5% to 2% of revenue. Management said it has not yet won competitive bids for subassemblies; Tejorup (10% stake) is developing a VSHORADS prototype.

segments.name: Exports / International
segments.commentary: Management said domestic drove most of Q1 growth because Q1 FY26 had large export orders; Turkey has turned out of loss, and UAE facility is expected to contribute revenue from Q2 FY27.

guidance_outlook: Management expects around 20% growth in FY27 and FY28 and continuing for 3-4 years, with an aim to double revenue in about three years.
EBITDA margin expected to rise 100-200 basis points over FY27 and FY28; management said Q1 margin should return to prior-year Q1 levels.
Management expects Q2 FY27 growth at similar levels to Q1, supported by seasonal monsoon-linked maintenance demand.
More than 80% of the INR209 crore order book is executable in FY27; customers are asking to prepone deliveries.
Railway (Vande Bharat, locomotives) revenue expected to convert within 9-12 months after workshop approval; management said new development items are a longer gestation cycle.
No new capex finalised; management wants to start the next expansion once newly installed capacity reaches 70-80% utilisation.
capex_capacity: Roughly INR100 crore expansion program across electrodes, wear plates and heavy engineering, with new strip slitting capability for backward integration.
Heavy engineering capacity being expanded from 9,000 to 18,000 metric tons (includes wear parts and flux-cored wires used internally); new Nagpur shop floor coming live in phases since Q1.
New capacity expected to contribute from the next quarter, but management said ramp-up will take 2-3 years; electrode capacity started in Q4 FY26 with similar 2-3 year ramp.
About INR67 crore of IPO proceeds still unutilised; management expects full utilisation by year-end, with savings to be redeployed subject to shareholder approval.
Units 1, 2 and 3 have no capacity change; utilisation there was described as 2-3% in one answer, while management said Units 1 and 3 operate at optimal levels.
demand_pricing: Finished steel production grew ~8.3% in April-June 2026 quarter; cement volume growth expected at 7-8% in FY27.

Named Q1 orders: INR9.88 crore VRM/separator parts (cement), INR8.16 crore roller-press rolls, INR10.63 crore roller assemblies, INR7.49 crore flux-cored wire (defence), INR26.31 crore RAPH rotor assembly (power); aggregate ~INR62.47 crore.
Raw material costs: steel up ~20%, some ferro-alloys like tungsten up several hundred percent; management said gross margin compressed by ~1-1.5% and customers have accepted higher prices.
Heavy engineering payment terms: 10-20% advance, 70-80% post-dispatch, balance after warranty documentation.
Top 10 customer concentration not disclosed on call; management said 60-70% expected, to be confirmed later.

qa_highlights.question: Growth drivers across consumables, wear parts, heavy engineering and trading; domestic vs export split?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth was 30%+ across the three segments, driven by a higher starting order book. Growth was mainly domestic because Q1 FY26 had large export orders that did not repeat.

qa_highlights.question: Raw material volatility and margin impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said prices remain high but volatility has eased and customers have accepted higher prices. Gross margin contraction was about 1-1.5%, with steel up ~20% and some ferro-alloys up several hundred percent.

qa_highlights.question: Executable portion of the INR210 crore order book in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: More than 80% is executable in FY27, and customers have asked to prepone some deliveries scheduled for next year.

qa_highlights.question: Share of profit from associate (LSN Diffusion) of INR4.4 crore: anomaly or steady?
qa_highlights.answer: Historical run-rate is INR1-2 crore per quarter, so management expects INR1-2 crore going forward and treats the rest of the Q1 amount as a one-off extra.

qa_highlights.question: FY27-28 revenue and margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects ~20% growth in FY27-28 and an aim to double in three years, with EBITDA margin up 100-200 bps over FY27-28.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone margin fall from ~18% peak to ~13%, and is Q1 the bottom?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said Q1 FY26 standalone PAT included a one-time ~INR5 crore subsidiary dividend. Management expects margins to return to prior-year Q1 levels and rise 100-200 bps over the next 1-1.5 years.

risks_watch: Raw material inflation persists: steel up ~20% and some ferro-alloys (tungsten) up several hundred percent; gross margin compressed ~1-1.5%, and management says the price levels remain high even though volatility has eased.
Margin recovery depends on new capacity ramp: management says new heavy engineering and electrode capacity will take 2-3 years to ramp, and new capacity contributes little EBITDA in the near term.
Q1 PAT includes ~INR4.4 crore share of profit from associate LSN Diffusion, of which management treats only INR1-2 crore per quarter as recurring; the rest is a one-off.
Railway and defence upside is still pending: railway workshop approvals are awaited, and defence is only ~1.5-2% of revenue with no subassembly bid win yet.

Top 10 customer concentration not confirmed on call (management said 60-70%, to be checked); the ~INR67 crore unutilised IPO proceeds are due to be fully used by year-end, with savings subject to shareholder approval.

Export recovery: Q1 domestic growth outpaced exports because Q1 FY26 had large export orders that did not repeat; management expects export ramp-up in subsequent quarters, and the UAE facility is due to contribute from Q2 FY27.

So, we are expecting to grow at around 20% in FY'27, '28 and continuously for next 3 years-4 years and we try to expect ourselves to double in next 3 years.
So, we are -- we always believe in , you know, overperforming and undercommitting or being realistic.
Honestly, we don't have that answer ready, maybe we can check from our ERP and send you a separate reply for that.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on order book visibility, FY27-28 growth of around 20% and Q2 growth, but was cautious and somewhat evasive on margins, raw material costs, and the sustainability of the associate profit. Several answers were deferred to follow-up (Top 10 customer share, exact raw material impact), and the CMD said the company prefers to under-commit and be realistic on guidance.

adds.what: Heavy engineering capacity raised from 9,000 to 18,000 metric tons (Nagpur shop floor, phased)
Roughly INR100 crore expansion across electrodes, wear plates and heavy engineering, incl. strip slitting capability

growth.why: Management guides ~20% revenue growth p.a. for FY27-FY28 backed by a INR209 crore order book (up 20.4% QoQ, >80% executable in FY27) and heavy engineering capacity rising from 9,000 to 18,000 MT, with a ~INR100 crore expansion in phases; the 20% figure is a multi-year aspiration with capacity ramp taking 2-3 years, so backing is partial rather than fully clear.
